correctness.rationale: The normalized exact-real interval map is an interval self-map. The independent rational replay bounded π using alternating Machin arctangent series and enclosed sine and cosine by Taylor polynomials with explicit remainders. Over the full closed parameter window it obtained derivative enclosures (2.623449645158,2.624057725237), (0.065750227349,0.068277048876), and (−2.781891716893,−2.781791848947). These signs and the strictly negative parameter derivative identify the endpoint combinations for the three cyclic images. Outward image bounds are (0.480731770791,0.480994300024), (0.941586540327,0.941605488212), and (0.163201402426,0.163285132726), strictly in the interiors of I1, I2, I0 respectively. The derivative product is in (−0.498411836327,−0.479837981840), contained in the stated strict interval. Thus f³ is a contraction of I0 into its interior, and the disjoint cycle boxes rule out period one, hence give primitive period three. The trapping intervals give an open neighborhood attracted to the cycle and the orbit exponent is negative. The rational endpoint checks are uniform, not rounded samples. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The trapping boxes do not quantify the full basin or the endpoints of the maximal periodic window.

value.rationale: Although the certified interval is narrow and not shown maximal, it is a rigorously established open periodic regime inside a specifically published no-window region for the same mathematical map. Attraction holds on an open interval of initial states, so the counterexample is not a lone repeller or a finite-iteration numerical anomaly. The value is the concrete counterexample to the global dynamical interpretation, without a cryptographic inference.
residual_risks: No implication about encryption security, global ergodicity, finite-precision or the absence of other invariant sets.
